conflicts.fact: Number of lessons in the sequence
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says questions will be answered across Lessons 2–6 and lists the topics (types, transmission, infections, prevention, economic importance); Lesson 4 calls itself part of an 'eight-lesson sequence'; Lesson 6 says open questions go to Lesson 7 for prevention and control, but prevention was already covered in Lesson 5 and Lesson 7 is a mould-conditions investigation.

Lessons 1-2 and 8 conclude the patches are fungal moulds; Lesson 5's prompt and explanation say the patches are 'fungi and bacteria' and colonisation by 'airborne fungal spores (and bacterial cells)'. Lesson 5 also says the colours are different mould species, while treating bacteria as part of the cause.

conflicts.fact: Number of containers in the investigation / conditions
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 Predict says eight sample containers across four conditions, but then lists containers A-F (six conditions) and the Observed section says six container conditions.

Lesson 7 says drying omena and salting meat reduce 'water availability and temperature', yet drying and salting do not lower temperature; Lesson 5 says refrigeration slows growth by reducing temperature.

Lesson 3 lists five routes (airborne, direct contact, respiratory droplets, contaminated water/food, vectors) with droplets separate from airborne; Lesson 5 uses four modes (direct contact, airborne/droplet, contaminated food/water, vector-borne), merging airborne and droplet; Lesson 4 uses airborne, waterborne, direct contact, bodily fluids.

conflicts.fact: Whether the patch fungi are the same group as beneficial microorganisms
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 asserts the patch organisms belong to the same broad group as those making yoghurt, which is made by Lactobacillus (bacteria); Lesson 2 classifies patches as fungal moulds, distinct from bacteria.
